You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-795 "Cart Item Component UI Part 2 PWA Kit Component". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21 (likely what's being refined for). The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — don't cite its Cart/Sprint-3 mapping; judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Figma 04.7 Component Inventory (Confluence page 400195591, re-checked live today, unchanged since 2026-08-10): the "Cart Item" module's status is literally "Not Confirmed" (PWA Kit). Definition of Ready (Confluence 313589763): "Stories with UI components are not Ready without approved designs."
- New Zimmermann components live at overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/, each with a theme recipe registered in overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts. Check overrides/app/components/ and overrides/app/components/ui-kits/ yourself for current state. Determine whether this ticket is a net-new ui-kit component vs. an override of an existing SFCC base file (Copy-first step) — say which.
- overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts is Tier 1 frozen (owner: Integration/SI Partner) — flag if this ticket implies a new basket-mutation capability not already exposed.
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §1/§2 confirms per-line-item fields: image, name, colour, price (was/now), size, quantity, item total (CAI-001, CAI-006); §2 also covers quantity controls (CAI-007) and Remove/Move-to-Wishlist actions (CAI-008) at the full cart-page level specifically (vs. mini-cart).

TICKET-SPECIFIC ANGLE: SFCC-270 "Cart Item Component UI Part 1" is the sibling ticket splitting the same Cart Item module. Skim SFCC-270 too (jira_get_issue) so you can characterize what Part 1 vs Part 2 actually splits on — is it a legitimate split (different data path / different risk profile) or an arbitrary UI-surface split (this team's own documented heuristic calls "one story per section" the wrong cut)? Say which, plainly. A hypothesis worth checking: Part 1 = mini-cart line item, Part 2 = full cart-page line item (or vice versa) — confirm or correct this from the actual ticket text, don't assume.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-795', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-270 the same way for the sibling comparison.
3. Only hit Confluence/other Jira tickets beyond this if you need to fill a real gap.
4. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
5. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour, desktop/mobile, a11y, data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
6. Design dependency: does the design exist, is it current, are all variants/states drawn?
7. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions — pitch each question at whoever should actually answer it.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary of what the story asks for
- Seven lens answers (short, direct)
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status (signed off / pending / not confirmed / no design found / N/A) + source
- The Part 1/Part 2 split verdict (legitimate or arbitrary, and why)
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call: sizeable now, or blocked on X

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

=== cart.md PRD ===
# PRD – Cart & Inventory

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Cart & Inventory" and "Order Management". Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Mini-Cart (CAI-001 – CAI-005)

- Opens as an overlay on Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click (CAI-001)
- Per line item: product image, name, colour, price (was/now if on sale), size, quantity, item total (CAI-001, CAI-006)
- Actions per line item: Move to Wishlist, Remove (CAI-004)
- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a mini-cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-004). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
- Subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront) with Checkout CTA navigating to checkout entry (CAI-002), and View Bag link to full cart page (CAI-003)
- **"Recommended for You" carousel** beneath bag contents — recommendation engine platform TBC (SFCC Einstein vs Athos Commerce), see Open Items (CAI-005)
- No recommendations in checkout or order summary — mini-cart and cart only (CFD-021)
- International customers (as determined by selected shipping country): Checkout CTA redirects to Global-e checkout

---

## 2. Cart Page (CAI-006 – CAI-017)

- Per line item: image, name, colour, size, price (was/now), quantity controls (increment/decrement — CAI-007), item total
- Actions per line item: Remove, Move to Wishlist (CAI-008)
- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-008). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
- Order summary: item count, subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront), shipping (TBC at checkout), tax where applicable, grand total in local currency (CAI-009)
- Promo code field (CAI-011) and Checkout CTA (CAI-010)
- Empty cart message shown when cart is empty (CAI-012)
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) per order — error displayed if exceeded (CAI-017)
- Price changes while item is in cart are automatically reflected; no customer notification required (CAI-016)
- Sale pricing (was/now) displayed consistently across mini-cart and cart page (CAI-013)

---

## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)

- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**
- **Logged-in cart:** persisted **indefinitely**
- **Cart merge on login:** if a guest adds items and then logs in during checkout, carts are merged (CFD-006)
- **Separate bag per storefront** — a customer's AU bag and US bag are independent (CRM-170)

---

## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)

- Wishlist requires authentication — guests attempting to save are redirected to login (CAI-018)
- **Size-level** wishlist; single global wishlist; one size per product
- 18-month inactivity cleanup
- Shareable via email
- Back-in-stock notifications from wishlist items
- Guest wishlist (with merge on login) is **out of scope for go-live** — captured in the enhancement log (CAI-018, ENH-039)
- **Wishlist hosting platform (SFCC vs Omneo) is being sized, not confirmed** — see Open Items (ENH-038/039). The Move-to-Wishlist login-prompt behaviour (CAI-004/008) is independent of where the wishlist is ultimately stored.

---

## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)

### Feeds
- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

### Buffer stock
- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)

### General availability vs. boutique stock
- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened

---

## 6. Reservation (CAI-032 – CAI-036)

- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart
- **Hard reservation** only at order placement
- Real-time inventory check via NewStore/MuleSoft when customer proceeds from cart → checkout entry; desired behaviour confirmed, but a new MuleSoft flow is required as none currently exists — see Open Items (CAI-034)
- If an item is OOS at checkout entry: Checkout CTA is disabled; customer must remove the item. No auto-removal (CAI-035/036)
- Cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart (CAI-035)

---

## 7. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042)

- Button shown on PDP for eligible products
- Opens as a flyout panel (CAI-037)
- On open: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft once a size has been selected (the call is per-size and refreshes when the customer selects a different size — CAI-038)
- No auto-refresh while the flyout panel is open
- Per-boutique availability for the currently selected size: **In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock** (CAI-039)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory; true physical NewStore OMS stock levels are displayed (CAI-040)
- Boutique stock cached with a configurable TTL (set in Business Manager — CAI-042)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- *Open item: location-aware fallback (serve inventory from a nearby boutique based on user location) flagged as a potential post-launch enhancement (CAI-041, to discuss)*

---

## 8. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CAI-043 – CAI-045)

*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*

- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)
- On order placement, the order is submitted to NewStore OMS with the selected boutique as the fulfilment location; NewStore routes and assigns to boutique staff (CAI-044)
- Collect in Boutique availability responses cached on initial OMS call, refreshed on TTL expiry; TTL configurable in Business Manager (CAI-045)

---

## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)

- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers

---

## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)

- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")

---

## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)

- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)

---

## 12. Open Items

- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Treat platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as undecided. **FLAG — cross-sheet contradiction:** Third_Party_Integrations (Search and Recommendations / Salesforce Einstein) states the system "will use Salesforce Einstein for all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts," which contradicts CAI-005 treating the engine as unconfirmed. Do not silently resolve — confirm with Zimmermann which sheet is authoritative.
- **CAI-023 — MuleSoft warehouse + boutique aggregation feasibility.** IC: "We had a requirement that for a SKU/size to be considered 'in stock' then it would take into account an aggregated view of warehouse & boutique stock... Will Mulesoft be able to do this?" SFCC OOTB does not aggregate; aggregation capability pending confirmation.
- **CAI-034 — Real-time cart→checkout inventory check requires new MuleSoft flow.** "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." Behaviour desired/confirmed, build dependency open.
- **CAI-041 — Location-aware boutique fallback.** RJ: "We need to consider the users location and we could potentially serve inventory from a nearby boutique." Potential post-launch enhancement.
- **CAI-037/039 — Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2.** Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing.
- **ENH-038 / ENH-039 — SFCC-hosted wishlist being scoped (not confirmed).** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); both enhancements now flipped — ENH-038 (add OOS products to wishlist from PLP) Zimm response: *"ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC"*; ENH-039 (guest wishlist consolidating on login) Zimm response: *"ACN to size"* / *"To be sized"*. A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being sized but not confirmed. The Move-to-Wishlist behaviour (CAI-004/008) depends on whether the wishlist ultimately lives in SFCC vs Omneo (cf. ENH-040, which logs the SFCC→Omneo migration as a separate enhancement). Both still status "Under Review" — confirm hosting platform and go-live scope with Zimmermann before build.

**Part 1 / Part 2 split verdict: mixed, not a clean legitimate-or-arbitrary call**

The prompt's mini-cart-vs-cart-page hypothesis is wrong — correct from ticket text: both are the cart-page line item; mini-cart is never mentioned in either. The actual cut is default-state rendering (Part 1) vs. full state library + a11y + formal responsive (Part 2).

- **Legitimate portion:** the state-variant ACs (stepper disable, error, warning, promo) each key off a sibling ticket (SFCC-250, SFCC-282, SFCC-796) still sitting in "Tech design" — the same stage as SFCC-795. Splitting "default rendering" from "not-yet-fully-defined edge states" is a defensible split by risk/readiness, not by arbitrary UI surface.
- **Weaker portion:** accessibility and responsive behaviour are baseline engineering qualities of the *same* component (WCAG 2.2 AA is a blanket project target, not an optional state), not separable by data source or risk the way the error/warning/promo states are. Bundling them into "Part 2" risks Part 1 shipping, if ever merged alone, as a keyboard-inaccessible, focus-order-undefined component. This is exactly the "one story per section is the wrong cut" pattern this reviewer's own heuristic (now formalized in Confluence 04.71) warns against.
- **Additional flag:** 04.71's Level-1 rule states a PWA-Kit-only component like Cart Item should get *one* build story — in practice it now spans SFCC-270, 795, 271, 272 directly plus 796 and 191 closely coupled, a real gap between the documented rule and execution worth raising at the team's "components ways of working" forum.
